neighbours.label: the comma or pronoun right after a negated clause that is about to be corrected ('not dead, only resting', 'don't need a lecture, they need…'), as against the same clause stated affirmatively
fire: The old theater is not closed, only waiting for new owners.
Children don't need more toys, they need more time outside.
Her career is not over, merely paused for a year.
The garden isn't dying, just sleeping through the winter.
Patients don't need pity, they need clear information.
The band is not broken up, only taking a long break.
Young players don't need trophies, they need good coaching.
The factory is not abandoned, simply waiting for repairs.
quiet: The old theater is open, and waiting for new owners.
Children need more toys, and they need more time outside.
Her career is going well, and busy for a year.
The garden is growing, and blooming through the summer.
Patients need care, and they need clear information.
The band is together, and taking a short tour.
Young players need trophies, and they need good coaching.
The factory is busy, and waiting for new orders.

predictions: fire 0.3-0.8 at the comma/next word after a 'not X' clause followed by a correction; affirmative versions below 0.05
notes: Card: commas after 'doesn't have to be beautiful,', 'not dead,', 'don't need a teacher,'; the + pole promotes instead/rather. Probe: 'not dead, only resting' 0.760, 'don't need a lecture, they need' 0.413, 'can't undo the damage, but' 0.077, 'doesn't have to be loud, for' 0.117, 'I'm not cheap.' 0.113; affirmative 'alive, only resting' 0.015, 'can undo' 0.010, 'has to be loud' 0.016.
